newsitem.title: CHINA: HK Exchange Fund assets hit HK$569 bln - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: HK Exchange Fund assets hit HK$569 bln - HKMA.

text.p: The total assets of Hong Kong's Exchange Fund were HK$569 billion at June 30, up 6.4 percent from December 31, 1996, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Thursday.
The official foreign currency reserves of Hong Kong, including those held in the Land Fund, exceeded US$82 billion at June 30, placing Hong Kong in fifth place in world rankings, the HKMA said.
"We are satisfied with the results which were achieved amidst difficult market conditions in the first half of 1997," HKMA chief executive Joseph Yam said in a statement.
The HKMA said foreign currency assets held in the Exchange Fund, excluding forward transactions, reached US$67.6 billion at the end of June, up from US$63.8 billion six months earlier.
The accumulated surplus of the Exchange Fund stood at HK$181.9 billion at the end of June, up 5.2 percent from December 1996.
Yam said the investment outlook for 1997 remained difficult.
"Forecasts on U.S. interest rates remain mixed and a strong U.S. currency may also adversely affect the non-U.S. dollar assets of the fund," Yam said.
